scenes.animation: Inside a space station, astronauts float around. A small yellow canary glides, loops and does backflips in mid-air, with no gravity to hold it down. Zippy tries to copy it and spins out of control.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: A bird in space? Isn't that against every rule?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It is! Meet Claribel, the canary from Feathered Friend by Arthur C. Clarke.

scenes.animation: A burly construction worker, Sven Olsen, sheepishly opens his jacket and the canary peeks out. The narrator and crew laugh. Claribel learns to fly in weightlessness, turning clumsy flaps into graceful stunts.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The story is told by a crew member on a space station. Sven Olsen, one of the best construction men, secretly brought a canary on board.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In weightlessness, Claribel learned to fly in ways no bird on Earth could. She became everyone's pet.

scenes.animation: One morning, Claribel floats limp and still in her cage. Sven gently holds her to an oxygen mask; she revives and flutters. Later she faints again, and the crew look worried and confused.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: One morning, Claribel was found unconscious. Sven gave her oxygen and she recovered.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Then it happened again. Nobody could understand why.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Is she sick? Is she homesick for Earth?

scenes.animation: A sepia flashback: coal miners carrying a canary in a cage deep underground. Back in the station, the narrator's eyes widen. A cutaway shows the station in Earth's shadow and a frozen pipe on the air purifier, with a silent alarm light.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Suddenly the narrator remembered that miners once carried canaries underground. If the bird fainted, it warned them of bad air.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: He raised the alarm. During an eclipse, part of the air purifier had frozen, and the warning alarm had failed.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Little Claribel had saved the whole crew.

scenes.animation: A theme card: a giant robot arm next to a tiny canary, and the canary wins a gold medal. Words appear: 'Nature can be wiser than machines', 'Observation saves lives'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: even in a world of high technology, a small living creature can be the best warning system.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: It also shows how curiosity and remembering old knowledge can solve new problems.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Language tip: the chapter practises talking about the future, using will, going to, and the present continuous.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. How did Claribel save the crew?' Answer flowchart: 'Claribel faints' → 'Miners' canary idea' → 'Air purifier frozen' → 'Crew saved'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: how did Claribel save the lives of the crew?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: her fainting warned of poor air. The narrator linked it to miners' canaries, and the fault in the air purifier was found.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: explain why the alarm didn't help. It had failed, so only Claribel could warn them.

scenes.animation: Recap board shaped like a space station window: '1. Sven smuggles Claribel on board', '2. She faints twice from bad air', '3. A tiny bird beats a failed machine'. Zippy salutes Claribel with a feather.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Sven secretly brings a canary to the space station.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: when Claribel faints, the narrator realises the air has gone bad.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: a tiny bird saves the crew when the machine fails.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Claribel for Commander! I'm voting twice.

name: Magnifying Glass by Walter de la Mare

scenes.animation: Zippy holds a round magnifying glass over an ordinary leaf. Through the lens, the leaf becomes a giant green landscape with rivers of veins. He jumps back in shock.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Whoa! This leaf has highways inside it!

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: That feeling of wonder is exactly what Walter de la Mare captures in his poem Magnifying Glass.

scenes.animation: The speaker, a curious child, moves a round glass over chalk, moss and a drop of water. Each one swells into a huge, detailed world full of shapes and tiny life.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In the poem, the speaker uses a round glass to look closely at ordinary things in nature.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Under the lens, tiny, everyday objects become large, detailed and magical, like whole little worlds.

scenes.animation: A spider spins a silvery web under the glass; every thread shines. A small fly buzzes too close and gets caught. The speaker watches, both amazed and a little sad.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The speaker watches a spider at work and admires how skilfully it spins its web.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: But the poem is honest too. The same clever web is a trap for flies.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Nature is beautiful and a bit scary at the same time.

scenes.animation: The magnifying glass grows into a giant telescope pointing at the night sky. The moon zooms closer and closer until a tiny cartoon figure seems to stroll across its surface.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: At the end, the poet imagines much stronger lenses. With them, even the distant moon would seem so close you could almost walk there.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The poem moves from the tiny to the huge, from moss to the moon.

scenes.animation: A devices board: 'Imagery: vivid pictures of tiny things', 'Contrast: small vs vast', 'Hyperbole: walking on the moon', 'Tone: wonder and curiosity'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Look for vivid imagery that helps us see small things clearly, and the contrast between the tiny and the vast.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Walking on the moon in an afternoon is playful exaggeration, or hyperbole.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: curiosity and careful observation reveal hidden wonders. Science and imagination work together.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. How does the magnifying glass change the way the speaker sees the world?' Answer blocks: 'Ordinary becomes extraordinary', 'Hidden detail and beauty', 'Sparks bigger curiosity'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: how does the magnifying glass change the way the speaker sees the world?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: it turns ordinary things into amazing worlds, reveals hidden detail, and makes the speaker dream of exploring further.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: in poem answers, mention the tone. Here it is full of wonder and curiosity.

scenes.animation: Recap board seen through a big round lens: '1. A lens turns small things into big worlds', '2. The spider's web: skill and danger', '3. From moss to the moon: curiosity grows'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: a magnifying glass turns tiny things into detailed worlds.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: the spider's web shows both skill and danger in nature.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: curiosity grows, from moss all the way to the moon.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: Next, I'm magnifying my homework. Maybe it'll look smaller.

name: Bibha Chowdhuri: The Beam of Light that Lit the Path for Women in Indian Science

scenes.animation: A night sky. One star in the constellation Leo twinkles brighter and a name tag appears beside it: 'Bibha'. Zippy squints at it through binoculars.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: A star named Bibha? Who's that, a film star?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: A real star of science. Bibha Chowdhuri, one of India's first women physicists.

scenes.animation: Kolkata in the 1920s and 30s. A determined girl studies by lamplight while others shake their heads. A signboard: 'Physics — few women allowed'. She walks in anyway, holding her books tight.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Bibha Chowdhuri was born in Kolkata in 1913. In those days, very few women were able to study science.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She studied physics anyway and began research on cosmic rays, tiny particles that come from space.

scenes.animation: An animated globe: a line flies from Kolkata to Manchester, England, with '1945'. In a lab, a scientist labelled 'Patrick Blackett' guides her. Cosmic ray streaks cross the screen like shooting stars.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: In 1945, she went to the University of Manchester in England. She worked under Patrick Blackett, a famous physicist who later won the Nobel Prize.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Her research on cosmic rays was widely praised. A newspaper called her India's new woman scientist.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: From Kolkata to Manchester, chasing particles from space. So cool!

scenes.animation: Back in India, she walks into the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) with a nameplate: 'First woman faculty member'. Years later, a star labelled 'HD 86081' is renamed 'Bibha' as the IAU logo glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Back in India, she became the first woman scientist on the faculty of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: She worked quietly, without seeking fame. Much later, the International Astronomical Union named a star Bibha in her honour.

scenes.animation: A theme card: a beam of light cutting through a dark path, with many young girls in lab coats walking along it. Word cards: 'pioneer', 'perseverance', and 'active: She studied cosmic rays / passive: Cosmic rays were studied by her'.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The theme: courage and perseverance can break barriers. Bibha was a pioneer, lighting the path for women in science.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: The chapter also practises the passive voice. She studied cosmic rays becomes cosmic rays were studied by her.

scenes.animation: An exam card: 'Q. Why is Bibha Chowdhuri called a beam of light?' Answer points: 'Studied when few women could', 'Important cosmic ray research', 'Inspired women scientists'. An 'Exam Tip' sticker glows.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Likely question: why is Bibha Chowdhuri called a beam of light?

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Answer approach: she succeeded in physics when women had few chances, did important research, and showed the way for others.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Exam tip: explain the metaphor. A beam of light shows the path to those who follow.

scenes.animation: Recap board lit by a star: '1. Born in Kolkata in 1913, she chose physics', '2. Cosmic ray research at Manchester', '3. A pioneer honoured with a star'. Zippy writes 'Future scientist' on his own lab coat.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Recap. One: Bibha Chowdhuri chose physics when few women could.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Two: her research on cosmic rays at Manchester won praise.

lines.speaker: NEO
lines.text: Three: a pioneer for women in science, she is honoured with a star.

lines.speaker: ZIPPY
lines.text: I'm a spark. Close enough to a star, right?
